twoParticipantLimit.threeCharacterRule: rotate speaker/listener pairs across lines; do not spawn a third world actor

lockStaging.framingChanges: use an explicit HardCut between shots
lockStaging.shotActorActions: When stage.lockStaging=true, the owning shot.actorActions MUST be empty.
lockStaging.authoringRule: When any dialogue line in a shot has stage.lockStaging=true, the owning shot.actorActions MUST be empty. Do not use Hold, FreezePose, Enter, Exit, Move, PlayAnimation, or any other world-actor action to keep a dialogue actor static. Dialogue visuals are controlled by the dialogue presentation fields only; place world-actor activity in a separate action shot before or after the locked dialogue shot.

layouts.distanceRule: active speaker is NEAR/larger; non-speaking listener is FAR/smaller; speaker changes reverse emphasis without changing identity

layouts.slotRule: speaker is primary Near; listener remains a secondary Mid visual

requiredness.structural: JSON Schema describes DTO shape and does not globally require conditional visual assets
requiredness.semantic: the presentation validator enforces background and participant visuals per preset; an explicitly exported allowsBuiltInParticipantFallback route counts as a legal identity-safe participant visual source
requiredness.subtitleOnly: SUBTITLE_ONLY is valid only when explicitly requested; automatic repair never silently downgrades to it

presentationSemantics.tupleRule: For new authoring, choose one exact compatibleTuples entry for the selected presentationPreset. Do not independently combine a legal layout, grammar and camera preset unless that exact tuple is exported.

newCutscene.chatGptUses: The ADD CATALOG package already loaded in the ChatGPT Project
newCutscene.output: For normal NEW authoring: one complete CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 JSON object. V5 remains the Unity backend and is used directly only for explicit legacy/revision/repair workflows.
newCutscene.unityBinding: CUTSCENE_SCRIPT_V1 contains semantic handles and creative intent; Unity resolves exact CURRENT asset IDs/routes and injects backend project/revision identity before V5 validation.

existingCutsceneRevision.ownership: Present State is current Cutscene state only; ADD CATALOG remains the global authoring/assets contract.

spatialComposition.backgrounds: Background/FarBackground Layer visuals are automatically fit with aspect-preserving Cover to the widest generated camera frame. Do not hand-tune scale merely to make a background fill the frame.
spatialComposition.actors: Generated world actors receive a bounded semantic base scale from renderer bounds, entity kind/role and the generated camera. Author scale values are hints/intent, not a request to compensate for source pixel dimensions.
spatialComposition.ui: Generated ShowUi/legacy UI defaults to screen-space semantic placement. Tactical/radar/scanner visuals prefer top-right; alerts prefer top-center; monitor/comms visuals prefer upper-right. Machine identifier payloads such as TACTICAL_RADAR are not rendered as giant visible labels when a visual asset is already present.
spatialComposition.midgroundForeground: Midground and Foreground visuals use bounded screen-coverage normalization separate from full-frame Background/FarBackground fitting, so a large source Sprite cannot accidentally swallow the shot.
spatialComposition.effects: World-space Effect visuals receive their own bounded visual baseline; procedural full-screen effects remain screen-space.
spatialComposition.principle: Author story intent and legal assets; Unity owns routine frame fitting and baseline visual normalization.

truthAlignment.rule: Catalog truth, ChatGPT authoring truth, normalization truth, validation truth and runtime truth must be identical for every authorable field.
truthAlignment.automaticRepair: A repair is successful only when it produces a canonical package accepted by the same validator. Half-repairs are forbidden.
truthAlignment.oneRoute: Prefer one explicit ownership route over legacy wrappers, hidden fallbacks or multiple competing activation models.

temporalOwnership.worldActor: WorldActor/Both permits a generated world object but does not make it visible from time zero. Generated actors begin inactive; Enter/Activate or the first visible world action activates for the sequence; Exit/Deactivate hides; sequence end returns inactive.
temporalOwnership.sequenceLayer: A layer authored in sequence.layers is sequence-owned and may persist for the sequence interval.
temporalOwnership.shotLayer: A layer introduced only by shot.layerActions is shot-owned and returns inactive at shot end. Shot actions that modify a sequence-owned layer do not shorten its sequence ownership.
temporalOwnership.uiVfx: Temporary generated UI and VFX are inactive before their interval, active only inside it, and inactive after it, including backward scrubbing and Evaluate().
temporalOwnership.principle: Generated state is a pure function of Timeline time plus authored ownership, not callback history.

effectAssetPolicy.proceduralRule: Procedural built-ins MUST omit assetId. IRONCLAD removes an authored assetId and records the canonicalization.
effectAssetPolicy.catalogEffectRule: All other Effect types use an exact Preview-safe Effect-primary assetId; unresolved content degrades to a visible yellow diagnostic placeholder.
effectAssetPolicy.uiSupportRule: Ui-primary generated support sprites are not authored into Effect assetId fields merely because they resemble an effect.

evaluationVsPlayback.evaluate: GenerateAtomic, scrubbing and PlayableDirector.Evaluate reconstruct deterministic state and never call real AudioSource.Play.
evaluationVsPlayback.playback: Actual runtime Playback evaluation may play audio when the bound AudioSource is enabled and active.
evaluationVsPlayback.playbackInitialization: MY_CutscenePlaybackController does not autoplay until Configure has completed and a PlayableDirector is bound.

debugIdentity.generatedVisual: Every generated visual exposes category, authored source ID, requested assetId, semantic type and owner ID in serialized debug metadata.
debugIdentity.placeholder: Unresolved visuals use bright yellow self-identifying diagnostics rather than anonymous gray rectangles.
debugIdentity.builtIn: Procedural visuals are explicitly marked builtInProcedural and named separately from catalog-backed VFX.

semanticCompositionPriority: Only then VFX, parallax and camera embellishment

runtimeContentSeparation.background: Environment only; do not choose baked dialogue/name/message art as a generic location background.
runtimeContentSeparation.dynamic: Speaker name, dialogue text, portrait and status/message content belong to runtime dialogue/UI fields.

dialogueEmotionVocabulary.emotionFields: stage.speakerEmotion, stage.listenerEmotion and delivery.emotion use MY_CutsceneDialogueEmotionV1 only: Serious, Shock, Anger, Perplexed, Sad, Happy.
dialogueEmotionVocabulary.paceFields: delivery.pace uses MY_CutsceneDialoguePaceV1 only: Slow, Medium, Fast. Semantic pacing such as Conversational, Measured or Natural must be mapped explicitly (currently to Medium) before serialization.
dialogueEmotionVocabulary.expressionFields: speakerExpression, listenerExpression and reaction.expression use the separate expression vocabulary. Put Determined/Concerned/Shocked/Relieved-style acting choices there, not in emotion fields.
dialogueEmotionVocabulary.safeImportAliases: Common unambiguous emotion words may normalize at the import boundary, but canonical ChatGPT output must use the six emotion values above.

assetSelectionDecisionOrder: The record must be legal for the exact destination field.
cutsceneSafeForPreview must be true for normal Preview authoring.
Prefer capabilities, tags and description that directly match the requested dramatic purpose.
Prefer human-reviewed records among equally suitable choices.
Never infer another use from filename, folder, path or appearance.

fieldPlacement.animationAssetId: Animation plus exact actor compatibleAnimationIds proof

dialogueBubbleSelection.selectionRule: Choose the best explicitly-described Preview-safe bubble for the speaker side and composition only when the presentation needs one.
dialogueBubbleSelection.fallback: When the preset does not require a bubble, use the canonical Dialogue Stage frame instead of forcing a random bubble.

cinematicMultiPlaneComposition.title: CINEMATIC MULTI-PLANE COMPOSITION
cinematicMultiPlaneComposition.rule: Prefer a coherent multi-plane composition when the Catalog provides materially useful planes; do not inflate an ordinary shot to an arbitrary layer count.
examples: space: starfield or planet, distant horizon, ship or architecture, restrained atmosphere
planet: sky or celestial distance, terrain, set dressing, foreground framing
interior: distant wall or window, room structure, actor support, foreground frame or haze
cinematicMultiPlaneComposition.familyRule: Prefer one coherent familyId/collection; mix only when the requested planes are materially compatible and the family cannot supply them.
cinematicMultiPlaneComposition.doNotFlatten: Do not label every Layer-primary asset Background when the reviewed metadata supports a more specific role.

layerRoleSemantics.FarBackground: Distant sky, starfield, planet, horizon or deep environment plane; usually behind Background and with smaller parallax motion.
layerRoleSemantics.Background: Primary environment or set plane behind the actor; use for the readable world context.
layerRoleSemantics.Midground: Intermediate set dressing, architecture or environmental plane between Background and Actor.
layerRoleSemantics.Actor: A layer-role label for an authored visual plane; it does not change cutscenePrimaryUse and does not make an asset Actor-primary.
layerRoleSemantics.Foreground: Near framing, occluder or edge decoration used sparingly so it does not obscure the focal actor.
layerRoleSemantics.Atmosphere: A Layer-primary haze, fog, glow or atmospheric plane in sequence.layers; Effect-primary VFX remains in effects.
layerRoleSemantics.Overlay: A Layer-primary authored overlay; it is not automatically Ui-primary.
layerRoleSemantics.Ui: A Layer-primary UI-like layer-role label only when the exact destination is a layer field; dedicated dialogue/UI fields still require Ui-primary.
layerRoleSemantics.canonicalRule: The destination field and cutscenePrimaryUse decide ownership. role never overrides primary use.

parallaxSemantics.scrollUses: Scroll consumes scrollUnitsPerSecond rather than parallaxFactor.
parallaxSemantics.factorMeaning: parallaxFactor is a multiplier on the authored Move/Parallax delta: 0 means no displacement, 1 means the full authored delta, and intermediate values are partial motion.
parallaxSemantics.default: MY_CutsceneLayerActionSpec.parallaxFactor defaults to 1; author 0 or another explicit value when the shot needs restrained depth motion.
parallaxSemantics.depthRelation: Distant planes generally move less than nearer planes; use the smallest motion that supports the shot and do not animate every layer.

sortingSemantics.relativeOrder: Use deterministic relative ordering: FarBackground behind Background, then Midground, Actor, and restrained Foreground framing.
sortingSemantics.foregroundRule: Foreground may frame the actor but must not obscure the focal actor without a deliberate authored composition.
sortingSemantics.uiOwnership: UI and transition presentation owns its canonical presentation order; do not invent a new magic sorting table.

dialogueStageRelation.lockedDialogue: A lockStaging dialogue line uses one explicit stage.backgroundAssetId plus its portrait/body/UI fields and optional stage.atmosphereVfxAssetIds.
dialogueStageRelation.richComposition: Use multi-plane layers for establishing or action beats; keep locked dialogue visually simple and line/stage-driven.
dialogueStageRelation.movement: When lockStaging is true, actorActions are empty and authored parallax/layer movement does not run under that locked dialogue beat.
dialogueStageRelation.atmospherePlacement: A Layer-role Atmosphere belongs in a Layer field; stage.atmosphereVfxAssetIds are always Effect-primary assets.

uiEventSemantics.showUi: ShowUi creates one generated CUTSCENE_UI presentation from an exact Ui-primary assetId. targetEntityId may be omitted; Unity deterministically binds it to ShowUi.eventId.
uiEventSemantics.hideUi: HideUi targets a ShowUi eventId in the same owner and normally omits assetId.
uiEventSemantics.visibility: If ShowUi.floatValue is positive it is the requested visibility duration. Otherwise Unity derives duration from the first later matching HideUi; without one, the presentation remains visible to the end of the owner.
uiEventSemantics.targetNamespaceException: UI event targetEntityId references generated UI event identity, not cast identity.
uiEventSemantics.failSoft: An invalid HideUi is optional and may be omitted with a yellow warning; it must not destroy an otherwise usable Preview.

shotPrinciples.intention: Give each shot one dominant intention or beat and set compositionTargetId when a focal entity is intended.
shotPrinciples.transitions: Use HardCut for a genuine framing reset; keep transitions restrained and motivated.
shotPrinciples.cameraMotion: Choose one dominant base camera action from Hold, Push, Pull, Pan, Track, Follow, Focus or Drift; Shake, ImpactShake and Recoil are additive beat support rather than a second base motion.
shotPrinciples.layerMovement: Move only the planes that communicate the beat; do not animate every plane by default.

failureBehavior.missingExactAsset: Choose the closest legal explicitly-described Preview-safe alternative.
failureBehavior.noLegalAlternative: Omit an optional element where possible; add missingAssets only when the contract requires it.
failureBehavior.storySafety: Do not silently change the core requested story unless required for a safe Preview.

technicalStableIds.scope: Every technical stable ID in the complete package is globally unique.
technicalStableIds.semanticIdentityException: Do not rename actorId, sequenceId, kitUseId or assetId merely to resolve a technical-ID collision.

worldActor.cast: cast[] declares identity and setup; it does not create a cinematic world actor by itself.
worldActor.presentationMode: Use exactly WorldActor, DialoguePortrait, or Both. Both explicitly permits world-action and portrait shots, but the representations must be temporally isolated.
worldActor.spawn: Legacy spawnWorldActor=true resolves to WorldActor only when presentationMode is omitted; it never infers Both.
worldActor.gameplayObject: If useGameplayObject=true is intentional, use that route and do not also create a duplicate cinematic actor.

warningVsError.yellowWarning: Recoverable and usable for Editable Preview without silently rewriting designer data.
warningVsError.blockingError: Invalid/unresolved required data, Unsafe content, incompatible placement, corrupted data, or a package that cannot be built or previewed safely.

serializationRules: Use exact serialized field names and exact canonical enum values.
Omit an optional string property when it has no value; do not emit null or an empty placeholder.
Emit every required string property with a non-null valid value.
Return one complete JSON object only; do not use Markdown or surrounding explanation.
assetIdRules: Use exact supplied assetId strings only.
Never reconstruct, shorten, guess a parent asset, or invent a fallback assetId.
Use only assets that the runtime resolver can resolve.
catalogRules: cutscenePrimaryUse is authoritative for Cutscene placement; do not infer placement from entityKind.
cutsceneSafeForPublish and cutsceneNeedsHumanReview retain publish-gate compatibility.
cutsceneReviewSeverity and cutsceneReviewReasons identify actionable metadata uncertainty.
authoringContract.snapshotIdentity: catalogRevision alone does not identify a complete ADD CATALOG snapshot. Compare catalogRevision, contractRevision, schemaHash and snapshotContentHash together.
validationRules: Unknown fields and unknown enum values fail validation with the exact JSON path and allowed values.
Validation accepts only canonical internal values after any listed safe input alias is normalized.

sequences.intention: Demonstrate one sequence, one shot and owner-local offsets.

shots.intention: Hold on an empty authored frame.
